convexnorm.essence: even for a rounder ball the crossing number ceiling holds, and it is exactly tight there
convexnorm.statement: for a strictly convex norm the crossing number bound still bounds unit pairs at a constant times n to the four thirds power, and valtr's construction attains that exponent

erdosguess.essence: the statement the whole course is about — believed by erdos, not yet known either way
erdosguess.statement: the erdosguess is that for all large n the unit pairs among any n points are at most n to the power one plus c over log log n, for an absolute constant c

flatarea.essence: a true fact about a different norm — the ceiling changes with the shape of the unit ball

genericnorm.essence: for a generic ball the count collapses to log squared growth — the far side of the norm family
genericnorm.statement: for most norms on the plane the unit pair count grows no faster than a constant times n times log n times log log n, and in d dimensions a comeagre set of norms stays below d squared times n times log squared n with a matching lower bound up to lower order

griddiag.essence: it tells the grid exactly which neighbor pairs are unit — the count two times m times m minus one falls out of it
griddiag.statement: among the points of an integer grid the unit pairs are exactly the horizontal and vertical neighbor pairs, for a diagonal step is never exactly one apart

kstbound.essence: the first ceiling on unit pairs — a power above one but below n squared

sstbound.essence: the sharper ceiling — the crossing number pushes the exponent from three half to four third
sstbound.statement: the spencer szemerdi trotter crossing number count pushes the unit pair bound down to a constant times n to the four thirds power

twosquares.essence: it is the seed of the leap — many equal-length lattice vectors come from many two-square writes
twosquares.statement: the products of numbers that are sums of two squares are sums of two squares in many ways

unitcircles.essence: it caps how many unit circles can share a point — the reason the unit pair graph is k23 free
unitcircles.statement: two unit circles with different centers meet in two points when the squared distance between the centers is below four, in exactly one point when it is four, and in no point when it is above four

unitpairs.essence: it names the quantity this whole course counts
unitpairs.statement: the number of unit pairs of a point set is the count of the pairs of its points that are exactly one apart
